findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-25: the key is correct (Node 24 with a stubbed fetch returning 400: the snippet prints 'Saved'). But the snippet's fetch POSTs JSON.stringify(draft) with no Content-Type header. html-css-js/fetch-and-browser-client/calling-your-spring-boot-api-from-the-browser/artifact.html teaches that exactly this call is sent as text/plain;charset=UTF-8 and that Spring answers 415, and item 28 in this bank tests the same fact. A learner who spots it may doubt the stem's '400 response', or suspect a second intended bug. No option uses it, so the key stays unique, but the code contains a taught defect that is unrelated to the question.
findings.recommendation: Add headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } to the fetch options on line 200, so the only defect is the ignored result object.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-12: the key is correct. In Chromium (Playwright route on http://staging.example.com), a Set-Cookie with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on a plain-HTTP response is not stored at all: the cookie jar stays empty and later requests carry no Cookie header. But the stem never says where the API lives. Distractor B (SameSite=Strict, line 96) is wrong only if the API is on the same site as the page, and its feedback assumes 'Requests the staging page starts to its own site'. If a learner pictures the API on another site, B is also a real cause.
findings.recommendation: State the API's location in the stem, e.g. 'the page and its API are both served from http://staging.example.com'. Optionally make the key feedback more precise: 'Browsers refuse to store or send a Secure cookie over plain HTTP.'

items.note: html-css-js-final-mcq-26 (lines 210-219) now ends the chain at catch, so no option depends on a then running after catch. The key needs only taught rules from the promises page: a then callback's return value becomes the next value, a throw becomes a rejection, and a rejection skips to the next catch. Node 24 prints 'B too big 6', matching the key at line 215; distractor feedback at lines 216-218 is accurate.
